name: C
typeSystem: Static and manifest, with many implicit arithmetic conversions and explicit pointer casts. C provides limited memory safety, and casts do not override rules such as alignment, object lifetime, and effective type.

typeSystemExample.caption: Generic max: no generics, so a macro is the closest equivalent

runtime: Compiled ahead-of-time to native machine code; no managed runtime or garbage collector.

runtimes.name: Native (GCC / Clang / MSVC)
runtimes.role: Standard path: compiled directly to the target CPU's machine code and linked with startup code and, in hosted environments, a C standard library.

runtimes.name: WebAssembly (Emscripten / clang --target=wasm32)
runtimes.role: Compiles C to WASM so it can run in browsers and WASM runtimes like Wasmtime.

runtimes.name: TCC -run
runtimes.role: Tiny C Compiler can compile to memory and immediately execute the resulting native code.

compilers.name: GCC
compilers.role: GNU Compiler Collection; a widely used C toolchain on Linux and embedded targets.

compilers.name: Clang
compilers.role: LLVM-based frontend with fast compiles and excellent diagnostics.

compilers.name: MSVC
compilers.role: Microsoft's compiler, the standard toolchain on Windows.

compilers.name: TCC
compilers.role: Tiny C Compiler; extremely fast, can compile and run in one step.

compilers.name: ICX
compilers.role: Intel's LLVM-based compiler tuned for x86 performance.

concurrencyModel: C11 defines a concurrency memory model, atomics, and an optional <threads.h> API. Programs also commonly use platform APIs such as POSIX threads; shared-state synchronisation remains explicit.

concurrencyExample.caption: 4 workers computing i*i in parallel via pthreads
